hypotheses: Does the optional incidence-angle branch help on held-out angle groups?
Does four-flip inference improve the same saved weights?

paired_comparisons.hypothesis: Add angle branch, four-flip inference fixed
Add four-flip inference, image-only weights fixed
Add four-flip inference, metadata weights fixed

interpretation.primary_cohort: Known-angle rows, matching test metadata availability; all rows also retained.
interpretation.variability: Two training seeds on identical folds; descriptive sensitivity, not confidence intervals. Split-seed variation is not measured here.
interpretation.component_scope: Adding the angle branch changes architecture and parameter count; this measures the branch as implemented, not a causal estimate of angle information alone.
interpretation.selection: All four conditions are reported. These post-development ablations are diagnostic, not an untouched final evaluation or a new leaderboard submission.
interpretation.budget: Both trained conditions use 5 folds x 2 seeds x 30 fixed epochs, identical training data/assignments/optimizer/augmentation. Metadata CV used two concurrent workers; image-only CV used one, with four threads per fit. Inference variants reuse identical weights.

independent_metrics.method: Independent NumPy binary cross-entropy from private OOF CSVs, joined to raw JSON targets, missingness and frozen fold IDs; not the package metric helper

notebook.visual_review: Both saved PNG outputs inspected: readable labels, common paired-effect scale, full legends and no clipping

public_comparison_recipe.difference: Descriptive name only after resolving device to cpu
